The Kibo Project — The more I try to write about this place, the more I feel words fall short.
I came across this medical centre very recently when a small pup, Lisa, met with a road accident. We rushed her there and were told that she would need complete cage rest and medical attention for around 15 days. At first, I was hesitant and anxious. So many questions kept running through my mind — Would they take good care of her? What if something went wrong? What if she didn’t recover well?
But today, after a week, I can proudly say that every one of my worries has been proven wrong, thanks to Ankita and the incredible team there (I’m sorry I don’t know everyone’s names). They have been taking such wonderful care of Lisa and giving her all the medical attention she needs. The improvement in her condition is already visible.
And it’s not just Lisa — the entire team looks after all the doggos and cattos there with so much love and dedication. I’ve honestly never seen such a clean and hygienic centre before. Everyone works tirelessly, round the clock, for the little world they have built for these animals.
Lisa has also made some adorable friends there — Bittey, Motor, Sarah, and Blackcurrant ❤️
Thank you so much to all of you, and kudos for the incredible work you’re doing. Much love!!!

featured_reviews.name: Rita Varma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I trusted Kibo with my cat, Chittu, for a few days of fluid therapy and oral medication, and it turned out to be one of the worst decisions I’ve made. I had heard good things about them, but my experience was nothing short of traumatic.

Throughout Chittu’s stay, getting updates was incredibly difficult. They only sent pictures after I repeatedly asked, and even those updates didn’t reflect the reality of what my baby was going through. A couple of days later, I noticed bruising in one of the photos, which made me feel something was seriously wrong so I went to pick him up.

What I saw broke me.
My cat had bruises in multiple places, even around the neck. He smelled strongly of urine, as if he had been left lying in it. His fur and skin were in terrible condition, and he was severely dehydrated. The updates they gave me were completely misleading compared to his actual state.

I had provided all his oral medications, yet they were returned to me unopened. This means none of his medications were given, which could have significantly contributed to his decline. His IV catheter wasn’t changed for days, causing phlebitis and bruising at the site, something that no responsible clinic should overlook.

Because of the condition Chittu was in when I brought him home, I was forced to make the heartbreaking decision of putting him to sleep. I cannot express the pain of knowing my baby could have had more time and comfort, but that chance was taken away from him.

Although I understood that my pet’s blood values didn’t indicate a good prognosis, I still believed he deserved every possible chance at recovery. Working in the medical field myself, I’ve seen many patients improve when the right line of treatment is followed. As a pet parent, my only wish was for him to receive proper care, comfort, and hygiene especially towards the end of his life.

Unfortunately, Kibo failed to provide even that basic dignity. What should have been compassionate, attentive care turned into a deeply disappointing and hurtful experience.

I trusted Kibo, and they failed my baby in every possible way. I will never forgive the negligence and lack of basic care that cost my cat his remaining time. I would not recommend this place to anyone who loves their pet.

featured_reviews.name: Sid Kolwankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
🐈 Flight of Pheonix 🐈

I found a this ginger kitten near Phoenix Mall, Kurla, in a very critical condition. He was barely able to walk, covered in flies, and refusing to eat. I reached out to several animal NGOs, but no one responded or picked up my calls.
Then I called Kibo Project, and to my relief, they immediately picked up and accepted the cat. I honestly didn’t think he would make it, but the Kibo team Riya, Abhishek, Vaibhav and Dr. Atharva showed incredible dedication. They kept me updated daily with photos and health reports of the kitten, whom I named Phoenix after the mall.
Over the next 18 days, I visited them a few times and even brought food for all the cats at their shelter. I’m so grateful that Phoenix fully recovered, was vaccinated and dewormed, and was released back near the mall yesterday, 3rd December.
The entire team’s commitment made all the difference. Thank you to Pragya for founding such an essential NGO. This world needs more people like you. I will always be thankful to Kibo Project for giving Phoenix a second chance at life.

People often don’t see this side of animal welfare—the effort, the risks, the emotional strength it takes. But this is what real change looks like. One dog at a time. One act of kindness at a time.

If we want a better world, it starts with how we treat those who have no voice.

We’ve been receiving a lot of enquiries for ownership and accountability trainings lately. And honestly, that’s a great sign.

And accountability? When something goes wrong, instead of blaming others, you accept it and quickly move towards finding and implementing a solution.
While its mainly about a mindset shift (and occasionally about the style of the leader), a few simple tools can really help.
One such tool is the RACI Matrix. It’s a popular project management tool which helps teams complete tasks more effectively by enhancing clarity on who will be playing which role during completion of each task. 
•	Responsible - Who is supposed to complete the task  
•	Accountable - Who has the final responsibility of completing the task
•	Consulted - Who’s inputs are to be taken to complete the task effectively
•	Informed - Which stakeholders are to be kept in the loop on the task status

Design Thinking Training for Innovation and Problem Solving

Have you ever felt your current problem-solving tools lacked something important? That they were a little lop-sided. More focused on logic and analysis and often missed out on the human and emotional aspect.  

Now that’s where Design Thinking comes in. A popular tool used extensively by organisations nowadays for a huge variety of uses. From solving complex problems, enhancing customer experience to even creating the next innovation. Design Thinking has got it all. It helps teams look at problems from the user’s point of view and find solutions that actually work. Its a practical yet human-centred approach that gives you the best for both worlds and offers a more holistic approach to problem solving. 

The process is as follows: 
1.	Empathize – Get deep into what the user really wants and needs
2.	Define – State the problem and objective in simple terms
3.	Ideate – Challenge what exists and generate new ideas
4.	Protype – Come up with possible solutions
5.	Test – Experiment to check the feasibility of the solution

Design Thinking helps teams think differently. It focuses on identifying real pain points, bringing people together to explore fresh perspectives and testing ideas to see what truly works.

customer_updates.name: Vijay Patil
customer_updates.text:
ज़रूरी सूचना / Urgent Notice
हिन्दी:
नमस्ते,
मैंने एक कुत्ते को देखा है जिसे तुरंत मदद की ज़रूरत है।
कुत्ते की स्थिति:
* वह बीमार दिख रहा है।
* वह अस्वाभाविक रूप से व्यवहार कर रहा था (मेरे पीछे आ रहा था, दूसरे कुत्तों पर हमला कर रहा था)।
* उसके मुँह से लार या झाग निकल रहा था।
* वह बहुत आक्रामक लग रहा था।
कृपया जल्द से जल्द इसकी मदद करें।
धन्यवाद।
English:
Hello,
I have seen a dog that urgently needs help.
Dog's Condition:
* It appears to be sick.
* It was behaving unusually (following me, attacking other dogs).
* There was saliva or foam coming from its mouth.
* It seemed very aggressive.
Please provide assistance as soon as possible.
Thank you.
मराठी:
नमस्कार,
मला एक कुत्रा दिसला आहे ज्याला त्वरित मदतीची गरज आहे.
कुत्र्याची स्थिती:
* तो आजारी दिसत आहे.
* तो असामान्यपणे वागत होता (माझ्या मागे येत होता, इतर कुत्र्यांवर हल्ला करत होता).
* त्याच्या तोंडातून लाळ किंवा फेस बाहेर येत होता.
* तो खूप आक्रमक वाटत होता.
कृपया लवकरच याला मदत करा.
धन्यवाद.

I found a small puppy on the road and took care of him for almost a month with proper food and attention. Trusting them, I handed him over for rescue, as they assured me of proper care, checkup, and vaccination.

This is extremely irresponsible and heartbreaking. Please do not trust them with any animal’s life. Animals deserve love and proper care, not neglect like this.

featured_reviews.name: Khushi Kachalia
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a stray kitten that no one was willing to adopt, her mom had died and we just picked her up off the street with no knowledge of how to care for her. We couldn't keep her because we could not transport her back to our home, and we already had a dog. She had fleas and worms and we were terrified about what to do for her. We called ARAS in the morning and they got back to us immediately and in the next 2-3 hours the founder came to pick her up. He even explained that you may video call the foundation or request pictures to check in on the animal. The work these people are doing is incredible, and the complaints about the request for donations is completely unjustified. Pets are expensive, these people are paying rent for a property as well as feeding, grooming, and giving medical care to over some 60 animals. A big thank you to Bhavesh Jain and everyone else working for this foundation ! As for Ginger, I hope someone will adopt her, she's very sweet, loves to cuddle and only 1.5-2 months old. There are pictures of her below, and if you are interested go ahead and give this number a call. 😄

featured_reviews.review_text: I had very good experience with my cat who underwent limb and tail amputation there. The doctors are very skilled and supportive. They communicated very well about our cat’s health. The supportive staff is well mannered. The person posted in our cat’s ward took good care. Theres decent cleanliness.

featured_reviews.name: Iminder Khurana
featured_reviews.review_text:
This animal hospital was constructed on the land donated by late Jamshedaji Tata. The building has terminus construed as dates back as 1888 and thus it carries a legacy of around 150 yrs.

The OPD is run by the government and administration and admission is private. The faculty are experienced but the care is just like a typical government run hospitals across the country.

The general ward has 4 to 5 tables (in the open) to handle and care the animals which doesn't require admission or for patients who can't afford.

Rest they have private wards with Ac rooms and some have even attached bath , incase your pet requires a longer and critical care.

One can see Feline , Canine , Bovine and all such animals and even Eagles and Hawks undergoing treatment.

Staff on Ground , ready to help.!

featured_reviews.name: YASH Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the best animal hospitals in Mumbai in terms of facilities and availability.  The caretaker staff are very supportive, humble, and kind. They handle the animals with care and try their best to help pet owners. Their behavior is polite and they make the environment comfortable.However, the doctors seem a bit careless at times. There were moments when proper attention  from the doctors felt lacking. Because pets are very important to their owners, careful examination and clear guidance from the doctors is very important.Overall, the hospital has good facilities and excellent caretaker staff, but the doctors need to be more attentive and responsible toward the animals .

featured_reviews.name: Melwin Gonsalves

My dog creatinine fell from 9.9 to 2.3 in 18 days. In any other hospital where would cost me 1-1.5 lakhs. Here it was done in 30% of the cost. It is definitely recommend however don't leave ur pet on hospital bharosa. Your the parent and stay with ur dog and trust me dog will get better.

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

featured_reviews.name: Kushagra karanje
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst place ever. Don't ever take your street dog or pet dog here. Here I am sharing my own experience. We saw an accident of a dog, the driver drove away immediately so me and my dad brought him here. He was literally very much injured. They asked us to deposit Rs5000 so we did and later they just kept him on stretcher and we were waiting for an hour to see how they'll treat him. They didn't even do anything. When my dad asked atleast do something it's close to an hour now. The hospital guy over there said ''AAMCHI KAMA AMHALA SHIKVU NAKA TUMHI JAVA IKDUN TEH KAI KARAICHA AMHI BAGHUN GHEU'' so me and my dad left in anger. Literally after 2 more hours they called us and said the DOG is DEAD and they also mentioned that we did number of tests of the dog     [ which was a lie] and its expenses were Rs3000. We will also do his funeral and that would amount you Rs 2000. So they did nothing and charged us Rs 5000. They didn't even tried to save that dying dog. Very bad experience of mine. So we always take such dogs to private doctors. Its way better. Please save yourself from these scammers.
